body.statement: For every \(0\le\varepsilon\le1/8\), with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\), the law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\). It satisfies \(P(T=0)=0.48\), \(P(T=1)=0.52\), \(\det(B)=0.6\), \(\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=0.4\), \(\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.06\), \(\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.4\cdot0.6\cdot36/169\), and \(\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}=0.4\delta_{0.25-\varepsilon}+0.6\delta_{0.25+\varepsilon}\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), all proxy matrices remain nonsingular, the quotient law is \(\delta_{0.25}\), and the latent weights remain unequal.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\varepsilon\in[0,1/8]\).  The Bernoulli probabilities in \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}class\text{-}witness}\) are valid because
\[
0.25\in(0,1),\qquad 0.5-\varepsilon\in[3/8,1/2],\qquad
0.5+\varepsilon\in[1/2,5/8].                                                  \tag{58}
\]
Conditional on \(U\), the construction makes \(X_2\) independent of \((Y(0),Y(1),T)\); since \(X_1=1\) and \(Y=Y(T)\), this gives \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\).  Conditional on \((U,T)\), it makes \(Z_2\) independent of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\), which gives \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(U,T)\).  It directly gives \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\), consistency, and the anchor.

Every realized \(X,Z\) is either \((1,0)^\top\) or \((1,1)^\top\), and \(Y\in\{0,1\}\).  With \(L=2\),
\[
\lVert X\rVert_2\le\sqrt2<2,\qquad
\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\lVert Z\rVert_2\lVert X\rVert_2\le2,
\qquad \lVert YZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2.                            \tag{59}
\]
Thus all retained sampling envelopes hold.  The four joint latent--arm probabilities are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &T=0&T=1\\ \hline
U=1&0.24&0.16\\
U=2&0.24&0.36
\end{array},                                                                  \tag{60}
\]
whose minimum exceeds \(\pi_0=0.1\); their column sums are
\[
P(T=0)=0.48,\qquad P(T=1)=0.52.                                                \tag{61}
\]
Directly,
\[
\det(B)=0.6,\qquad \det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=0.4.                                  \tag{62}
\]
For a real \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix \(G\), \(\sigma_1(G)\sigma_2(G)=|\det G|\) and \(\sigma_1(G)\le\lVert G\rVert_{\mathrm F}\), so
\[
\sigma_2(G)\ge\frac{|\det G|}{\lVert G\rVert_{\mathrm F}}.               \tag{63}
\]
Here
\[
\lVert B\rVert_{\mathrm F}^2=2.68,\qquad
\lVert A_0\rVert_{\mathrm F}^2=2.58,\qquad
\lVert A_1\rVert_{\mathrm F}^2=2.685.
\]
Since \(0.6^2/2.68>0.1^2\) and \(0.4^2/2.685>0.1^2\), (62)--(63) imply the proxy rank margin \(\min\{\sigma_2(A_0),\sigma_2(A_1),\sigma_2(B)\}>0.1\).

From (60)--(61),
\[
w_0=(1/2,1/2),\qquad w_1=(4/13,9/13).
\]
The proxy factorizations give \(M_t=A_t\operatorname{diag}(w_t)B^\top\), and taking determinants yields
\[
\det M_0=0.4\cdot\frac14\cdot0.6=0.06,
\qquad
\det M_1=0.4\cdot\frac{36}{169}\cdot0.6.                                   \tag{64}
\]
The specified outcome means give
\[
\tau_1=0.25-\varepsilon,\qquad \tau_2=0.25+\varepsilon,
\]
and hence
\[
\nu_{P_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{wit}}}
=0.4\delta_{0.25-\varepsilon}+0.6\delta_{0.25+\varepsilon}.                  \tag{65}
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), (65) aggregates to \(\delta_{0.25}\), while (60), (62), and (64) are unchanged and the underlying weights remain unequal.  Equations (58)--(63) verify every member property of the repaired \(\mathcal M\); (61)--(65) prove the remaining assertions.
body.justification: The explicit interior witness rules out an apparent collision phenomenon caused by collapsing proxy rank or treatment positivity.
body.gap: The VMW paper does not provide this unequal-weight, exact-effect-collision submodel; the proposition is a construction check rather than a stand-alone statistical advance.
body.consumer: The witness is the early kill test for the modulus and the common base point for both local lower-bound regimes.
